correctness.rationale: The polar is the cyclic octagon with vertices (1,0),(1,t),(t,1),(0,1) and negatives, including degenerate edges at endpoints. For matrix rows r,s, exact inversion gives ||L^-1||=M(r,s)/|det L| with M the maximum of four sums of two absolute values, while ||L||≤1 puts both rows in the polar. Scaling rows separately to its boundary cannot increase M/|det|. The 48 nonexceptional edge pairs have single-branch certificates L_h−(1+t/2)det≥0, separately affine in edge parameters; its four corner polynomials are Bernstein-positive on eight rational t subintervals. Independently executed the symbolic coefficient check for all 13,824 rational entries. Remaining 16 edge pairs are reduced by swap/sign/row symmetries to three explicitly analyzed representatives; their averaged bounds, monotonicity, and concavity work for all 0≤t≤1. Upper map k=t/(2+t) has ||L||=1 and ||L^-1||=1+t/2. Handles both endpoints and arbitrary invertible real L, not just symmetry-respecting maps. Finite rational certificate represents continuum polynomial positivity, not sampling.
